# Kotoba

## The Kotoba stack

Safe code. Trusted state. Controlled execution. Kotoba Labs is building toward the default safe and ultra-fast stack for AI-generated software.

- Kotoba: the language — https://kotoba-lang.org/
- Graph & Ontology database: content-addressed graph state and knowledge — https://graph.kotoba.cloud/ (agents: https://graph.kotoba.cloud/llms.txt)
- Kotoba Cloud: identity and deploy control for the execution environment — https://kotoba.cloud/

Speed claims apply only to the published workload, artifact, and qualification gates. Safety claims retain their trusted computing base and residual risks. Kotoba Cloud discovery is live; hosted apply is not yet offered.

> Kotoba is a small, Clojure-shaped, security-first language for capability-confined AI-agent programs. Its public compiler emits WebAssembly and denies ambient host authority.

Canonical site: https://kotoba-lang.org/
Public operator: Kotoba Labs Inc. Public contact: support@kotoba-lang.org. Sales contact: Ryo Awai.
Language authority: https://github.com/kotoba-lang/kotoba-lang
Compiler and CLI: https://github.com/kotoba-lang/kotoba

- Bounded Amu/Rust/C/Zig/Go/Swift native comparison status: https://kotoba-lang.org/benchmarks/runtime-native-latest.json
- String/collection/allocation/I/O/concurrency/real-app observations: https://kotoba-lang.org/benchmarks/domains-latest.json
- 2026-08-30 implementation update: bounded native vector scalar replacement, POSIX NEON/SSE2 checked string equality, root-confined async filesystem capability, bounded structured concurrency, and public Kotoba CLI native KEXE compilation are implemented. These postdate the current domain benchmark and are not yet ranked speed evidence.

## Navigating Kotoba source as an agent

Kotoba source is S-expressions, so a definition is identified by its structure rather than its name or file. `kotoba-lang/symbol-index` (https://github.com/kotoba-lang/symbol-index) indexes every top-level definition in a checkout (`.kotoba` / `.cljk` / `.cljc` / `.cljs` / `.clj`) and answers in one call and a few hundred tokens what a full-file read costs about 6,580 tokens on average (measured 2026-09-15):

- `symbol-index <sym>` — where it is defined; up to three exact hits print the definition head, so no file read follows
- `symbol-index <file.cljk>` or `<ns>` — outline: line, signature and a structural `#hash` per definition (same hash = same body; names, local binding names, comments, docstrings and whitespace are not part of it)
- `symbol-index find <sym> --dependents [--depth N|all]` — every definition that references it, by depth: what to re-check before changing it (alias-qualified references that grep does not see)
- `symbol-index closure <ns/sym>` — Merkle closure hash with the dependencies' bodies folded in; a memo key for compile and test results
- Exit codes: 0 hit, 1 measured zero, 2 refused (`REFUSE<TAB>reason`). Run it at the project root; never `build` in `$HOME`.

Install from the checkout with `kbb --backend sci scripts/install.cljk` (symlinks `symbol-index`, installs the Hermes skill). Measured on 2026-09-17 with Hermes Agent over 10 queries (lookup, dependents, closure): skill preloaded, 10/10 correct, 1.5 tool calls, 2.5 API calls and 0 file reads per query. The same day, Claude Code with only a one-line "consult the index before reading" instruction scored 9/10 at 6.1 tool calls — an agent that does not know the `--dependents` / `closure` entry points falls back to grep; that is why they are listed here. Numbers and reproduction are in the repo's `measurements.edn`.

## Minimal verification

On macOS or Linux with Homebrew:

```sh
brew tap kotoba-lang/kotoba
brew trust kotoba-lang/kotoba
brew install kotoba
kotoba selfhost check --json
```

Without Homebrew (a sandboxed or unattended agent that may write only inside
its worktree and may not install packages): the release archive is one static
executable. Download `kotoba-<darwin-arm64|darwin-amd64|linux-amd64>.tar.gz`
and its `.sha256` from https://github.com/kotoba-lang/kotoba/releases/latest/download/,
verify the digest, extract into `.kotoba-toolchain/` (gitignored, ~42 MB), and
call `.kotoba-toolchain/kotoba` by path — section 1b of agent-quickstart.md
(measured 2026-09-17 on macOS arm64, v0.7.3, environment reduced to `PATH`,
`LANG`, a private `HOME` and `TMPDIR`). A shell with no network cannot fetch
it; do not report later steps as passed then.

Then follow agent-quickstart.md to compile a zero-import Wasm module and execute its exported `main`. Treat a `planned` / `adapter-required` response as a plan, not evidence that code ran.

## Security assessment

- https://kotoba-lang.org/blog/infra-cost-measured-path/ : Mechanisms and named numbers only for build wait, CPU wall time, artifact bytes, and JVM-free emit. No $/month savings, no language Release URL, no Kotoba-beats-Rust-or-C on GPU. English is the source of record.
- https://kotoba-lang.org/blog/csf2-attack-graphs/ : Selected NIST CSF 2.0 contributions, six defensive attack stories, source evidence and operational gaps. Not certification or a live penetration test. Available in the seventeen site languages.
- https://kotoba-lang.org/security/csf2-threat-model.md : Detailed English threat model, inspected source revisions, trust boundaries and local verification scope.
